title: Biduality at the point
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting),
let $C$ be a perfect point complex. The
evaluation and coevaluation give a canonical isomorphism

$$
C\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C^{\vee\vee},
$$

and for every object $D$ of the category at the point, the canonical
tensor–internal-Hom comparison

$$
C^\vee\otimes_A^LD\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,D)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the module target categories at the point in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and the coefficient rings of [def-pod-conventions]. First work at one finite, integral, or finite-field stage, writing its commutative coefficient ring as $A$. By [def-pod-perfect-point-complex] choose a bounded cochain complex $P$ of finite projective $A$-modules, zero outside $[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $QP\cong C$ in $D(A)$. Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The argument below works for any $D\in D(A)$, so in particular for every object of the specified full point subcategory. The common-stage algebraically closed coefficient category is treated in steps 7–8.

Regard $A$-modules as module sheaves on the one-object site with bottom topology, as in [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map] (take the ring map to be $\operatorname{id}_A$). Evaluation at the unique object identifies these sheaves and all their module operations with ordinary $A$-modules. Put $E=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,A[0])$, using [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Its term $E^r$ is $(P^{-r})^*$ and it vanishes outside $[-b,-a]$. By [lem-sf-finite-projective-dual] these terms are finite projective. Apply [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] to $P$ and to $E$. It gives the natural representative identifications
$$QE\cong (QP)^\vee,\quad Q\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(E,A[0])\cong (QP)^{\vee\vee},\quad Q\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,N)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(QP,QN)$$
for any complex $N$. In particular the maps to the Hom complexes formed with a K-injective replacement of the second variable are quasi-isomorphisms: by naturality their localizations are the displayed comparison isomorphisms followed by the image under derived Hom of a quasi-isomorphism. These are precisely the Hom-representative hypotheses of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps].

For the tensor calculation choose, by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], a K-flat representative $N$ of $D$ with flat terms. By [lem-pc-perfect-ring-dual-term-flat], every term of $E$ is flat on the one-object ringed site. Since $E$ is bounded above, [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $E$ K-flat. Both $E$ and $N$ therefore satisfy the flat-term K-flat hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], which gives
$$Q\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_A N)\cong (QP)^\vee\otimes_A^L D.$$
It also identifies the tensor product in the other order. These identifications are natural and compatible with changing the representatives.

proof.text:
Under step 2's identifications, [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] represents the canonical bidual map by the chain map
$$\delta_P:P\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(E,A[0]),\qquad x\longmapsto\bigl(\phi\longmapsto(-1)^{p|\phi|}\phi(x)\bigr),\quad x\in P^p.$$
Only $|\phi|=-p$ contributes, so its component in degree $p$ is $(-1)^p$ times ordinary module evaluation $P^p\to(P^p)^{**}$. This evaluation is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-finite-projective-dual]. Thus every component of $\delta_P$ is invertible. The component inverses form a chain map, by multiplying the chain-map equation by the inverses on each side. Hence $\delta_P$ is a chain isomorphism and its image is the required canonical isomorphism $QP\to(QP)^{\vee\vee}$.

Apply [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-degrees] to $P,N$. It supplies degreewise isomorphisms
$$t_n:\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_A N)^n\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,N)^n$$
which on $E^r\otimes N^s$, $r+s=n$, have only the Hom coordinate $p=-r$, where
$$\phi\otimes y\longmapsto\bigl(x\longmapsto(-1)^{rs}\phi(x)y\bigr).$$
The hypothesis of [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-differential] is exactly this normalization, so the $t_n$ commute with the differentials. They give a chain isomorphism $t:\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,N)$, since the degreewise inverses commute with the differentials as well. All hypotheses concern $P$; neither result requires boundedness of the chosen $N$.

proof.text:
Identify this particular chain isomorphism with the canonical comparison. The total-tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives a chain isomorphism $\sigma:E\otimes N\to N\otimes E$ by $\sigma(\phi\otimes y)=(-1)^{rs}y\otimes\phi$ in degrees $r,s$. Indeed both $d\sigma$ and $\sigma d$ equal
$$(-1)^{rs}d_Ny\otimes\phi+(-1)^{rs+s}y\otimes d_E\phi,$$
and swapping twice is the identity. The map $e_{QP,D}$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] is represented on $N\otimes E$ by $y\otimes\phi\mapsto(x\mapsto y\phi(x))$. Its composite with $\sigma$ has exactly the signed formula in step 5. Equality follows on every pure tensor and every Hom projection, hence on the entire complexes. Consequently the canonical map $(QP)^\vee\otimes_A^L D\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(QP,D)$ is $Qt$ under steps 2–3 and is invertible. The naturality of both canonical maps in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], together with the natural representative comparisons of step 2, transports both conclusions along $QP\cong C$ and the chosen representative of $D$.

For algebraically closed coefficients use the common-stage point category of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. Represent $C$ and $D$ over finite coefficient fields $E_1,E_2$ and choose their finite compositum $L$. By [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting], every object of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E_1)$ is perfect, so $C$ has a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ already over $E_1$. Its extended terms remain finite projective: a finite generating surjection $E_1^m\to P^i$ splits by projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and tensoring the splitting gives a retraction of $L^m$. Thus steps 1–6 apply over $L$. The stage functor sends these two isomorphisms and their inverses to isomorphisms in the common-stage category: the two inverse equations hold already over $L$ and hence in its Hom colimits.

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, applied at one finite coefficient field; common-stage interpretation of def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category

proof.text:
The stage images in step 7 are the specified canonical maps, as can be checked on the same representatives. For a field extension $L\subset M$, the map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_L(V,W)\otimes_L M\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_M(V\otimes_LM,W\otimes_LM)$$
is the coordinate identity for $V=L^m$, and restriction to a split summand proves it for every finite projective $V$. Apply this to the finitely many nonzero terms of $P$ and of $E$: the relevant Hom products are finite in each degree, so these identifications commute with the Hom differential and with the displayed evaluation formulas. Tensor associativity identifies the scalar extension of the tensor complexes; the scalar extension of $t$ and of $\delta_P$ has exactly the same signed formulas over $M$. They therefore define the same comparison and bidual maps at every later common stage. The transition maps and composition in [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] now show independence of the common field and of representatives. This proves both clauses also for the common-stage coefficient category of [def-pod-conventions].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q66-63cb21f3f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 18 cited node statements, the blueprint text in master, main-20261015 and main-20261017, and Stacks 07VI (more-algebra.tex l.19175 ff.) together with the tags it cites. The statement is the blueprint's, unchanged. The point categories are full subcategories of D(A) for commutative A, plus the common-stage Qlb category. The proof follows 07VI: the termwise dual E=Hom(P,A[0]) is a bounded complex of finite projectives; lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model applied to P and to E gives, by naturality in N, the Hom-model quasi-isomorphisms that lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps requires; E is K-flat by 06YQ. For the bidual, only one degree contributes, with sign (-1)^p, and I checked this by hand on A--a-->A in degrees 0,1. For the tensor map, t (degrees lemma plus differential lemma) equals the e-chain map composed with the Koszul swap; I recomputed the swap's differential identity, so e is invertible whatever symmetry convention is used. At Qlb, lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting gives perfectness, the stage functor preserves the inverse equations, and step 8 (marked elementary) checks the finite free/retract scalar extension; I accept it as elementary. No new nodes, no cycle, proof_deps match the uses, no SGA. I accept all 10 declared tool_uses as generic black boxes; unit sk-def-perfect has no steps, so no route is replaced. The blueprint proof's truncation step is wrong as written (τ^{≤i}/τ^{≤i-1} is H^i[-i], not P^i[-i]); the maintainer may record this. The report wrongly says main-20261015 has no proof, which does not affect the delivery. No fixes.
